edges.reason: Both quotes state that Pirro's office withdrew/dropped the charge against Mr. Hearn. NYT (NEW) uses "withdrawing the charge against Mr. Hearn" and The Hill (EXISTING) uses "moved to drop the charge". They describe the same event.

confirmations.label: “Ms. Pirro’s office dramatically reversed course on Friday, not only withdrawing the charge against Mr. Hearn but blasting the Interior Department for the rushed and “botched” renovation, along with U.S. Park Police officials who fed bad information that led her to publicly cite “tremendous evidence” against Mr. Hearn.”

edges.sentence: On 2026-10-06, The Hill reported “Pirro moved to drop the charge weeks later after evidence from the Interior Department showed Hearn did not cause the damage, and that the issue stemmed from problems with the pool’s multi-million dollar renovation and accelerated efforts to complete the project ahead of America’s 250th birthday celebrations.”; on 2026-08-03, The New York Times reported “Ms. Pirro’s office dramatically reversed course on Friday, not only withdrawing the charge against Mr. Hearn but blasting the Interior Department for the rushed and “botched” renovation, along with U.S. Park Police officials who fed bad information that led her to publicly cite “tremendous evidence” against Mr. Hearn.”.
